items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: this guy at MCA, Bob Wooling, said, 'Look, you shouldn't be fooling around with this gig. Why don't you play the Palladium.'

ctx.x: I wasn't you know, but he was very jealous and drunk all the time, and he thought something was going on, and what was going on was she'd had it with him and he was looking to blame anybody he could blame. So I got out of that scene. And I had this little band I put together, with Buddy Childress, like I told you. We came back and we played the El Rancho and some other places, and we went up to Alaska. We were up there for two weeks, up in Anchorage. And if I'd have stayed up there another week I think I'd have…

was in that band and Paul Sarmento and Buddy Childress, and Boone Stines was the drummer, a guy out of Oklahoma, a guy that had a good beat but no technique. And then I -- this guy at MCA, Bob Wooling, said, "Look, you shouldn't be fooling around with this gig. Why don't you play the Palladium." I said, "They won't let me in with a mixed band." He said, "You don't have a mixed band. You don't have any band. What are you talking about?"
